annotation_notes: SECOND HELD-OUT SET. The first held-out procedure
test the moment its failures were used to fix the extractor. This one is
annotated blind, before running the extractor against it, to obtain an
Structurally novel: a CASE EXPRESSION inside an assignment — a construct
absent from all three previously measured procedures.
Consistency of principle over convenience: in the tiered-interest
procedure each IF/ELSIF tier was annotated as its own rule, because each
threshold is a separately changeable policy. The same reasoning applies to
each CASE branch here, even though the extractor is unlikely to decompose
them. Annotating them as one rule would flatter the tool.
